newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool's medium-term outlook good - broker.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool's medium-term outlook good - broker.

text.p: The outlook for the wool market over the next few months was much more positive than at the same time last year, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said in its monthly Wool Watch report.
Fundamental factors of improved demand from overseas mills, combined with favourable exchange rate conditions and continuing low levels of supply, were all encouraging, Wesfarmers said.
Although volatility was a fact of life in the wool market, it was expected that prices would remain around current levels in the coming months, it said.
Australian wool's eastern market indicator closed at 716 cents a kg clean on July 4 before the end-season recess, up sharply from 598 cents a year before.
Market buoyancy would be next tested when spring shearing clips came to auction in September causing increased supply, Wesfarmers said.

The outlook for finer 19 micron to 21 micron wool was for strong demand, the outlook for 22 micron-24 micron wool was firm in the short-term, while the outlook for 25 micron-30 micron wool was steady, Wesfarmers said.
